traps_new: 116. `KeygenZintCall.region start count` covers keygenLines indices start-1..start+count-2, i.e. source-file lines start+3..start+count+2 (keygenLines[0] is file line 4). Verify every piece boundary by grep before pinning: a misaligned piece fails its parse and falls back to `getD skip`, making `only`/shape audits pass VACUOUSLY. Always state piece audits as `map ... = some` (the Depth0 pattern) so a failed parse cannot pass.

117. A comment line starting `|--` inside a match-alternative list tokenizes as the `|` alternative marker plus a line comment and breaks the equation compiler. Write `-- ` comment lines between alternatives.

118. A `some`/constructor application split across a layout-sensitive newline inside `do`-match alternatives can elaborate as a bare `some : Option Unit` statement and poison the following pattern compilation. Keep constructor applications on one line or bind the tuple to a named `let` first.

119. `fresh`'s fallback chain serves both statement and for-clause positions. Statement-position pointer binds (`u0 = u;`, `f += fstride;`) must consume their `;` (pointerStmt); for-clause binds (`x = xx`, `x += xstride` in rebuild_CRT's loop clauses) must leave the ending token for `clauses`. `pointerExpr` accepts ANY token as a name, so an unguarded pointer clause can misparse a scalar assignment.

120. A diagnostic probe must exercise the real `parseStatement` path, not `fresh` alone: word-layer statements (assignment/store/return/for/if) fall through `fresh` by design and only parse at the statement level.

121. Monolithic `by decide` over a ~300-line body parse exceeds kernel memory (traps 88/95/98 family). Bind in statement-boundary pieces with a chained scaffold and a line-partition theorem, then compose only/callShape/bitcastCount via rfl equations (`only_seq`/`callShape_seq`/`bitcastCount_seq`) and literal `decide` at the end; `simp only` + `try decide` silently re-reduces the parse when a rewrite misses and panics the kernel instead of failing softly.

122. `Eq.trans` direction in `some`-injection derivations: from `both : map p = map (some part)` and `rhs : map (some part) = some (f part)` conclude `some (f part) = some v` via `(both.trans rhs).symm.trans hs`.
